thread:
anya: Quick follow-up from the kernel-selection RFC — I sketched a small 'control-plane safepath' that standardizes per-model enablement + fallback ordering. Wanted feedback before I turn it into a short RFC patch.

matt: Nice phrase :) high-level — is safepath just a config object in model-metadata or a runtime-only routing override?

lena: If it's runtime-only we risk drift between control plane and offline tooling (evals, perf tests). prefer model-metadata with an explicit 'runtime_overrides' section.

anya: Good call. My draft keeps canonical intent in model-metadata and exposes a mutable control-plane layer for temporary rollouts / emergency disables.

samir: So final fallback order will be: kernel-pref -> per-model override -> global fallback? Need something deterministic.

anya: Exactly. Deterministic rule: 1) model pinned kernel list, 2) per-model control-plane override (percent/region), 3) global compatibility list, 4) last-resort safe-kernel.

matt: How do we express percentage rollouts? We should avoid complex sampling inside kernels. Suggest control-plane stores rollout spec: {pct: 10, key: "user_id%100"} and runtime reads a stable hash.

anya: Agreed. Sketch:
```yaml
model_metadata:
  kernels: ["fast-attn", "qkv-compat"]
  safepath_overrides:
    - scope: region:us-west-2
      rollout: 20
      kernels: ["fast-attn"]
```

lena: Need audit logs for all control-plane changes. If we flip a kernel for a customer, we must show who did it and when. Also TTL for overrides.

samir: Metrics to track during rollout: token p50/p99, rejected-token-rate, kv-cache-miss-rate, and increased GPU util. Also track model-level correctness metrics from eval hooks.

anya: Yes — plan is to wire rollout rigs into existing tracing and a small 'regression alert' that checks eval prompts each minute. If regression > threshold, emergency rollback triggers.

runtime-bot: Canary deployed safepath override to us-west-2 (10%): rollout_id=rp-2026-04-02-1

deploy-bot: Note: we should add a kill-switch label that operators can flip without going through control-plane DB writes. Maybe a redis key TTL that bypasses safepath lookups.

matt: I worry about two sources of truth: redis kill-switch + control-plane overrides. We need priority rules and strong invariants. Suggest kill-switch always wins but requires 2-person review to set for customer-facing changes.

anya: Proposal: immutable priority order: operator_kill > control-plane_override > model_metadata > global_default. Implement operator_kill as signed short-lived tokens, not plain redis keys.

lena: For offline tooling, include a read-only endpoint that returns effective safepath for a model+region+customer as-of timestamp. That helps reproduce experiments.

samir: Also include a small telemetry label on tokens so we can attribute infra cost to rollout variants.

anya: I'll update the draft with these changes and add the telemetry schema + TTLs. If anyone has objections call them out now, otherwise I'll open the PR tomorrow. :thumbsup:

matt: No objections from me. Please add tests for deterministic sampling and a sim that pushes 1M hashed keys to verify distribution.

lena: +1 on tests and audit logs. Also add a migration plan for existing model_metadata entries (compat defaults).

samir: OK, thanks. Happy to help wire the alerting rules.

anya: Thanks all — will ping when the PR is live.
